note: **Seven columns, and two kinds of cell.** A form this archive has actually met in one of its records is evidence. A form it has not met is a **lookup aid** — the right thing to type into a Hungarian or a German index tomorrow, and nothing more — and it is marked. The split is not decided by hand: `scripts/name-forms-audit.py` looks every form up in the roster, the register, the households, the burials, the headstones and the four FamilySearch harvests, and the build refuses if the marking drifts from what the records say.

slipnote: A form in the six columns above is a **language's** form of a name: a different people saying the same thing. A slip is not. **A slip is one clerk, once** — a J read for an I, an r read for an n, a Z heard as a K — and it matters more, because a language form can be looked up and a slip can only be recognised. Every one below is a spelling this archive actually met in a document, with the document named.
shape: THE ESTATE'S SHARED GIVEN-NAME SHAPE, adopted 17 September 2026 and taken from the Blazevic archive, which is the only one of the two that could hold what both knew. This archive held the same knowledge as seven comma-separated strings per row, which can carry a form and nothing about it. Here each form carries the number of times this archive has MET it, so the difference between a record and a lead is in the data rather than recomputed by a page. Converted mechanically from givennames.json and checked against this archive's own gate: 645 forms, 419 attested, 226 aids, all three exact. A SLIP IS NOT A LANGUAGE'S FORM OF A NAME and keeps its own key, as it always did here.
filename: It is givennames-forms.json and not names.json, because names.json in this archive is the SURNAME file - variants, distribution, the 1945 census - and a first pass at this overwrote it. Caught by the build, in a component two pages away.
